acceptance: A tracked dependency approval registry exists and every current root npm direct external dependency has exactly one exact-version approval with purpose and license posture; there are no stale/duplicate approvals.

The validator fails closed for unapproved external direct dependency, exact-version mismatch, semver/range/floating declaration, malformed approval, duplicate approval, stale approval, unsupported ecosystem, and missing purpose/license posture.

Cargo path/workspace dependencies are distinguishable from external registry/git dependencies. Any external direct Cargo dependency requires an approval; registry dependencies require an exact pinned version; cargo metadata --locked evidence is checked when a real external Rust graph is present.

Current LICENSE_POLICY is not silently broadened. MIT and Apache-2.0 posture is accepted per policy; other expressions require an explicit separately governed policy exception rather than an agent guess.

Dependency validator conformance suite contains negative fixtures for unapproved npm/Cargo dependencies, version/range drift, lock-resolution mismatch, stale/duplicate approvals, and license-policy mismatch and those negatives demonstrably fail validation.
The existing branch-protected Provenance workflow runs the dependency validator tests and repository check on pull_request and main before any Diffcipline policy migration occurs.
Slice A merges and its post-merge Provenance job is SUCCESS while .diffcipline.toml still says dependency/lockfile REVIEW.

Only after Slice A post-merge qualification, Slice B changes Diffcipline dependency_manifest_changes and lockfile_changes to allow, with governance docs explaining that executable dependency judgment moved to the already-required Provenance gate rather than being removed.

After Slice B, an ordinary non-dependency PR still receives the same Diffcipline size/scope/untracked/verification enforcement, while an unapproved dependency fixture fails the required Provenance dependency validator.
Branch protection required-check set remains JavaScript / TypeScript, Rust, SpecGrain, Diffcipline R1, and Provenance; enforce_admins remains enabled; no bypass evidence is used.
PR #54 remains unmerged during this prerequisite. Its prior Diffcipline REVIEW/failing required job is preserved as negative evidence, not rerun or rewritten into PASS.

Exact implementation passes validator tests, repository dependency check, project/provenance checks, pnpm check, git diff --check, Diffcipline R2 for each non-dependency governance slice, protected exact-head CI, and post-merge qualification.

minimality.rationale: Use Python stdlib plus existing package/Cargo tooling inside the already-required Provenance job; do not add a dependency merely to review dependencies, and do not add a new protected-check name when the existing Provenance gate can own this repository-governance concern.

requirements: Never merge or bypass a dependency change while Diffcipline REVIEW is still a required failing check.
Never change Diffcipline dependency/lockfile policy to allow before the required Provenance dependency gate is merged and post-merge green.
Never remove a required branch-protection check or disable enforce_admins as part of this repair.
Never silently broaden license admission beyond canonical LICENSE_POLICY.
Never represent dependency admission validation as vulnerability, SBOM, signature, or release-security proof.

outcome: Kernux can admit legitimate npm/Cargo dependency and lockfile changes only when an already-required Provenance gate deterministically validates exact approved direct dependencies, lock consistency, bounded purpose, and license posture; only after that gate is proven does Diffcipline stop treating dependency files as an unconditionally unmergeable REVIEW.
rationale: The first Rust contract dependency exposed a governance deadlock: Diffcipline v1 intentionally returns REVIEW for any dependency manifest/lockfile change, its Action preserves exit 1, and protected main requires that job with enforce_admins=true. Diffcipline v1 has no review-approval hook and enterprise policy is monotonic, so a legitimate reviewed dependency cannot currently merge. Bypassing branch protection or relabeling REVIEW is forbidden. The safe repair is to establish a deterministic dependency-admission check inside the already-required Provenance job first, prove it on main, then migrate Diffcipline dependency/lockfile handling to ALLOW because judgment has moved into an executable required gate rather than disappeared.

risk.recovery: Before policy migration, revert the validator/gate slice normally. After migration, recovery restores Diffcipline dependency/lockfile REVIEW before removing or weakening the Provenance dependency gate. No product runtime or user data is created.

scope_in: Create a machine-readable dependency approval registry covering direct external npm and Cargo dependencies with ecosystem, package name, exact admitted version, scope/purpose, license posture, and approval rationale. Internal workspace/path dependencies are not external approvals.

Create a dependency-free Python 3.11+ validator using stdlib JSON/tomllib/subprocess that reads package.json, the Cargo workspace/member manifests, lock state, and the approval registry. It must fail closed on unapproved external direct dependency, version drift, non-exact direct version, malformed approval, duplicate approval, stale approval, unsupported ecosystem, or missing purpose/license posture.

For npm, require root direct dependency/devDependency versions to be exact and match approvals. Bind pnpm lock consistency through frozen installation in existing CI; validator must still prove every declared direct external npm package has exactly one matching approval.

For Cargo, recognize registry/git external direct dependencies versus workspace/path/internal dependencies; require exact registry versions for approved direct external crates, match approvals, and use cargo metadata --locked when an external Rust graph exists to verify the committed lock resolves the direct package/version and expose resolved license metadata.

Apply current LICENSE_POLICY admission: MIT and Apache-2.0 are permitted subject to provenance/notice obligations; any other SPDX expression/class remains explicit review unless a dependency approval records a separately governed license-policy exception. Do not silently broaden LICENSE_POLICY.

Add focused conformance tests for valid npm baseline, unapproved dependency, version mismatch, floating/range version, duplicate/stale approval, malformed registry, internal path dependency, Cargo locked resolution mismatch, and non-approved license posture using bounded temporary fixtures rather than changing real manifests.

Integrate dependency validation and its test suite into the existing required Provenance CI job while leaving .diffcipline.toml dependency_manifest_changes=review and lockfile_changes=review unchanged in the first implementation slice.

After the dependency-admission gate is merged and post-merge qualified on protected main, perform a separate policy-migration slice changing only Diffcipline dependency/lockfile decisions from review to allow and updating governance docs to state that dependency judgment is now enforced by the required Provenance dependency gate.

Prove the migration does not weaken net governance: required Provenance remains branch-protected; dependency validator rejects a deliberate unapproved dependency fixture; Diffcipline continues enforcing size/scope/untracked/verification rules; no branch protection bypass or required-check removal occurs.

Document the current first-Rust-dependency blocker and recovery path so PR #54 remains unmerged until this prerequisite is proven and its branch is updated from canonical main without rebase/force-push.
scope_out: Do not merge, bypass, or relabel PR #54 while Diffcipline returns REVIEW.
Do not add serde/serde_json or any new product dependency in this governance prerequisite.
Do not change project licensing, donor-import rules, branch protection required checks, or Provenance semantics unrelated to dependency admission.
Do not treat automated dependency approval as security/vulnerability/SBOM/release qualification; later security/release phases own those stronger controls.
title: KX-P01-S05-T01 prerequisite — Replace unmergeable dependency REVIEW with enforced dependency admission
